"Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate. Job gains have been solid on average, while inflation remains below 2 percent and market-based inflation compensation is low. In line with reaction-function evidence in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler, holding the funds rate at 1.5–1.75% is consistent with policy smoothing when inflation undershoots and output is near potential. The coexistence of low unemployment and subdued inflation is also consistent with expectations-centric models (e.g., Rudebusch and Svensson) and term-structure evidence (Ang and Piazzesi) suggesting anchored long-term inflation expectations and a flatter Phillips curve. The Committee’s emphasis on weak business fixed investment accords with investment literature showing sensitivity to financial conditions and financing constraints (investment spending amplified by credit markets; links to work associated with Gertler). Operationally, T-bill purchases and repo operations to maintain “ample reserves,” together with IOER and ON RRP settings, reflect modern floor-system implementation (Goodfriend, 2002) aimed at stable policy transmission rather than balance-sheet-driven stimulus. Overall, the tone is mildly positive on real activity but cautious/dovish on inflation."
